use_policy.title: Use policy
use_policy.banner_text: AlloViewer is an experimental software tool. It is not certified or approved for clinical diagnostics, treatment decisions, transplant allocation, or patient management.
use_policy.research_text: AlloViewer is provided for research use, method development, teaching, and workflow evaluation. The software is not intended to replace established laboratory procedures, expert review, or validated clinical decision pathways.
use_policy.no_clinical_text: Outputs generated by AlloViewer must not be used as the sole basis for clinical diagnosis, donor-recipient compatibility assessment, transplant eligibility, organ allocation, treatment decisions, or patient management.
use_policy.review_text: All results require independent review by qualified laboratory or clinical experts. Users are responsible for checking input data, assay quality, control performance, software output, and any downstream interpretation.
use_policy.validation_text: Users are responsible for validating AlloViewer in their own laboratory setting before any operational use. Users are also responsible for complying with applicable institutional rules, quality-management systems, data-protection requirements, and regulatory requirements.
use_policy.liability_text: The authors and developers do not accept responsibility for clinical, regulatory, operational, or financial decisions made on the basis of unvalidated software output. Use of the software is at the user's own risk.
use_policy.data_text: Users should not upload identifiable patient data unless they have the required legal, institutional, and ethical basis to do so. Uploaded files should be reviewed and de-identified where appropriate before use.

about.title: About AlloViewer
about.purpose_text: AlloViewer is a web-based software platform for standardized and traceable interpretation of HLA antibody diagnostics. It supports automated analysis of image-based complement-dependent cytotoxicity (CDC) assays and flow cytometry crossmatch (FCXM) data, with the aim of reducing operator-dependent interpretation in physical HLA antibody testing.
about.workflows_text: AlloViewer currently supports three assay workflows: CDC-based HLA antibody specificity analysis using commercial test-cell panels (CDC-PRA), CDC crossmatch analysis, and FCXM analysis. In CDC-PRA, well-level cytotoxicity patterns are mapped to the uploaded test-cell panel layout to support inference of candidate HLA antibody specificities. In CDC crossmatch assays, donor lymphocyte wells are scored for cytotoxicity after incubation with recipient serum. In FCXM, uploaded .fcs files are analyzed by automated population detection and population-specific IgG readouts.
about.why_text: CDC and FCXM assays remain relevant in histocompatibility testing, but their interpretation can depend strongly on manual review. Microscopic CDC scoring is often semi-quantitative, while FCXM analysis commonly depends on manual population gating and expert-defined fluorescence interpretation. AlloViewer provides fixed, reproducible analysis steps so results can be compared more consistently between operators, runs, and assay formats.
about.how_text: For CDC microscopy, AlloViewer uses full-resolution image analysis with a simulation-trained U-Net model to detect lymphocytes. Detected cells are classified using experiment-specific positive and negative controls in red-green fluorescence space, allowing well-level cytotoxicity scoring and explicit handling of uncertain cells. For FCXM, AlloViewer applies quality control, lymphocyte selection, marker-informed population detection, and gate-specific IgG signal extraction. Each workflow is exposed through an assay-specific web interface and API-based access.
about.dev_text: AlloViewer was mainly developed by {{cassian}} (Institute for Transfusion Medicine and Immunohematology, German Red Cross Blood Donation Service Baden-Württemberg-Hessen, Frankfurt) and {{tarik}} (Division of Rheumatology, Department of Medicine V, Heidelberg University Hospital) in a collaborative project (for the full author list see our paper).
about.license_text: AlloViewer is made available under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License (CC BY 4.0), unless stated otherwise. The current version is intended for research use and workflow evaluation. It has not been established as a stand-alone clinical decision system, and prospective multi-center validation is required before routine clinical decision support.

cdc_pra.title: CDC-PRA analysis
cdc_pra.intro: Use this workflow for CDC-based HLA antibody specificity analysis with a commercial test-cell panel. AlloViewer maps the observed cytotoxicity pattern to the uploaded panel layout and reports candidate antibody specificities.
cdc_pra.step1_body: Start by uploading the .xlsx plate layout. The file should describe the test-cell panel and the HLA typing linked to each well. The layout is required because CDC-PRA results are interpreted from the pattern of positive and negative wells across the panel. You can download the example file below to check if you have the same layout. Please use the official layout from the company, whereever possible.
cdc_pra.step2_body: Upload the folder containing the microscopy images for the plate. Images are mapped by their order in the uploaded image list against the selected scan order. Although file names are used for sorting, please carefully check the image mapping table before starting the analysis.
cdc_pra.step3_title: 3. Review the plate and image mapping
cdc_pra.step3_body: Review the well roles, scan order, and image-to-well mapping. Make sure each uploaded image is assigned to the correct well. The analysis should only be started when the expected number of wells is mapped and no required images are missing.
cdc_pra.step4_title: 4. Run analysis and review the output
cdc_pra.step4_body: After starting the analysis, AlloViewer segments lymphocytes, classifies cells using positive and negative controls, and calculates well-level cytotoxicity values. The output includes the plate result, well-level values, quality indicators, and a summary of inferred reactivity patterns that can be compared with the uploaded panel layout.

cdc_xm.title: CDC-XM analysis
cdc_xm.intro: Use this workflow for image-based complement-dependent cytotoxicity crossmatch analysis. AlloViewer processes microscopy images of donor lymphocytes incubated with recipient serum and reports cytotoxicity readouts by well and cell mode.
cdc_xm.step1_body: Upload the folder containing the CDC-XM microscopy images. Wells can be assigned as sample, positive control, negative control, IgM control, or empty. The IgM control is used to check whether Dithiothreitol (DTT) treatment effectively reduces IgM-mediated reactivity, helping separate IgM-related signal from clinically relevant IgG-mediated complement activation.
cdc_xm.step2_title: 2. Review plate layout and column modes
cdc_xm.step2_body: Check the well roles and column modes before running. T means T cells, B means B cells, and T/B means that both T-cell and B-cell results are represented for the selected column mode. Adjust the layout if the default plate scheme does not match the experiment. Then check that images are mapped to the correct wells.
cdc_xm.step2_alt: CDC-XM plate layout and column modes
cdc_xm.step3_body: When all wells, controls, cell modes, scan order, and image mappings are correct, start the analysis. AlloViewer detects individual cells, classifies viable and lysed cells using internal controls, and calculates well-level cytotoxicity fractions.
cdc_xm.step4_body: After processing, review the plate preview, well status, cytotoxicity values, and summary table. Borderline or unexpected wells should be checked manually, especially if the control wells or IgM control suggest assay problems.

fcxm.title: FC-XM analysis
fcxm.intro: Use this workflow for flow cytometry crossmatch analysis from .fcs files. AlloViewer supports automated panel extraction, sample assignment, population detection, and population-specific IgG readouts.
fcxm.step1_body: Upload the folder containing the .fcs files. After upload, assign files to the correct sample cards. A negative control is required. Positive controls can be added if available, and sample cards can be added for patient or test samples. Display names can be shown as file names or tube names, depending on the available FCS metadata.
fcxm.step1_alt: FC-XM FCS upload and sample assignment
fcxm.step2_body: AlloViewer reads the marker panel from the uploaded .fcs files. Review the detected channels, antibodies, marker roles, and target populations before running. At least one IgG marker should be selected, because the final FC-XM interpretation depends on population-specific IgG signal extraction.
fcxm.step3_body: Start the analysis after the samples and panel are checked. AlloViewer performs quality control, lymphocyte selection, marker-informed population detection, and gate-specific IgG readout calculation. The results view lets you select a sample, file, and gate to inspect scatter plots, IgG density curves, and per-population metrics.
fcxm.step4_title: 4. Set report rule and download summary
fcxm.step4_body: After the run is complete, choose the positivity metric and threshold used for the report. Available metrics include median ratio, median shift, fluorescence index, and percent positive cells. Download the summary only after checking that the selected gate and sample-level results match the intended interpretation rule.
